raw.source: US BIS - Department of Commerce Rescinds Biden-Era Firearms Rule, Restoring Common Sense to Export Controls on Civilian Firearms
raw.content_en: BIS has rescinded the Biden-era firearms export rule, easing licensing and classification treatment for civilian firearms and ammunition under the EAR. Exporters of sporting shotguns, rifles, and related parts should re-verify ECCN/Commerce Control List classification, confirm whether items move from State Department ITAR jurisdiction back to EAR Commerce jurisdiction, and update license determinations accordingly. Reassess end-user/end-use screening, country-based restrictions, and recordkeeping obligations before shipping. Note that rescission does not eliminate restricted-party, embargo, or UN arms embargo screening duties, and Section 301 tariffs plus HTS classification still apply to physical shipments.
raw.content_zh: 美国商务部工业与安全局（BIS）撤销了拜登时期的枪支出口规则，放宽了民用枪支弹药在《出口管理条例》（EAR）下的许可与分类处理。出口运动霰弹枪、步枪及相关零部件的企业应重新核实ECCN/商业管制清单分类，确认相关物项是否从国务院ITAR管辖回归商务部EAR管辖，并相应更新许可判定。发货前需重新评估最终用户/最终用途筛查、国别限制及记录保存义务。注意：规则撤销并不免除受限方、禁运或联合国武器禁运筛查义务，实体货物仍适用Section 301关税及HTS归类要求。

checklist.desc: Confirm whether civilian firearms, shotguns, rifles, and parts now fall under EAR jurisdiction and identify the correct ECCN or EAR99 status after the rule rescission.
Determine if items previously under State Department USML jurisdiction have shifted to Commerce jurisdiction; document the jurisdictional basis and retain analysis.
Re-run license requirements by destination and end user; assess eligibility for license exceptions and update the export authorization in your compliance system.
Screen consignees, end users, and intermediaries against BIS Entity List, Denied Persons List, and OFAC SDN; confirm no UN arms embargo or country embargo applies.
Classify shipments at 10-digit HTS level (e.g., 9302, 9303), check Section 301 list exposure, and document country of origin and value build-up.
Obtain and retain non-transfer and end-use certificates from foreign buyers; keep records per EAR Part 762 retention requirements.
